rationale: Evidence from iteration 9 (score 237.3, best so far): oval finishes 11 of 20 with progress 0.80, but s-bend (progress 0.105) and slalom (0.078) still stall at about 0.1 progress and end off track, with max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Raising kp from 4.5 to 5.0 barely moved s-bend (0.110 to 0.105) and slalom was unchanged, so steering gain is not the binding limit on those tracks. Earlier evidence says speed is: dropping base_speed from 1.4 to 1.1 raised s-bend progress from 0.045 to 0.19 and oval progress from 0.32 to 0.67. Iteration 5 (base 1.0) was confounded with kp and kd changes and regressed, so the speed trend is not yet fully tested below 1.1. Oval has time margin (mean finish 1.72 s against a 3 s limit), so a modest speed cut should cost little there. Change: base_speed 1.1 to 1.0, the only change from iteration 9. Geometry and gains are unchanged so the speed effect can be read cleanly. Expected result: s-bend progress rises clearly above 0.15 and slalom above 0.1, with oval completions holding near 9 to 11 of 20 and completion_time rising only slightly. Hypotheses: (H1) if s-bend and slalom still stall at about 0.1 with max_error at 0.06, the failure is not speed-limited and the next step is sensor placement (y) or kd. (H2) If oval completions drop below 8 of 20, the speed cut is too costly for finishing and base_speed should return to 1.1 with a different lever. (H3) If all tracks survive but none finish, base_speed should be raised slightly, to about 1.05. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness.
